description: Field-site records. Every fact carries an evidence_status (unverified | mapped | field_confirmed | lab_confirmed), its source and retrieval date. Nothing here was inferred from proximity, imagery alone, or assumption.

records.name: Allen Branch
records.campus_reference: Somerset Community College, main campus, 808 Monticello Street, Somerset, KY 42501
records.access_notes: Campus access route, permission requirements and a safe entry point have not yet been documented. Until faculty publish them here, visit only with a faculty member.
records.safety_notes: Do not enter the water during or after heavy rain, when flow is high or the water is turbid. Wear gloves when handling water, sediment or biofilm, and wash hands afterward. Do not touch or collect surface scums or thick mats. Watch footing on wet rock and banks, and keep track of road crossings and culverts. Report any dead fish, animals or unusual scums to faculty rather than sampling them.

facts.label: Stream name
facts.source: USGS National Hydrography Dataset (name and GNIS ID carried on the NHD flowline)
facts.notes: Aliases: none recorded. Local or historical names have not been checked.

facts.label: Campus center point
facts.value: 808 Monticello Street, Somerset, KY 42501 — the center of every portal map (37.05979, −84.61690)
facts.source: Kentucky 911 Site Structure Address Points (Pulaski County 911 record, updated 2022-05-03), via KyGovMaps
facts.notes: An address point, not a surveyed campus location. The U.S. Census Geocoder places the same address 268 m to the northwest by street-range interpolation; the 911 address point is used instead.

facts.label: Distance from campus center to the mapped stream
facts.value: About 250 m (straight line) to the nearest point of the NHD Allen Branch centerline; the mapped line extends to about 2.2 km away
facts.source: Computed from the two mapped datasets above (911 address point; USGS NHD flowline)
facts.notes: Straight-line map distance only — not a walking route, an access point, or a field measurement.

facts.label: NHD feature type
facts.source: USGS NHD high-resolution flowline, reach code 05130103001019
facts.notes: A map classification. Whether the stream flows year-round, seasonally or only after rain has not been observed and is a research question.

facts.label: Mapped length
facts.notes: Length of the mapped centerline only; unmapped headwater channels are not included.

facts.label: Mapped flow direction
facts.value: Generally west to east along the mapped line, toward its junction with Sinking Creek

facts.label: Downstream connection (mapped)
facts.value: Allen Branch → Sinking Creek (perennial) → Pitman Creek → Lake Cumberland (Cumberland River)
facts.source: USGS NHD flowline network traced downstream reach by reach; Lake Cumberland identified as NHD waterbody GNIS 00490483 (reservoir)
facts.notes: This is the mapped surface path. It has not been walked or verified. In this karst setting, part of the flow may move underground, and the name 'Sinking Creek' itself hints at sinking streams. Do not treat the connection as established for any flow condition until field-checked.

facts.label: Subwatershed (HUC 12)
facts.source: USGS Watershed Boundary Dataset; the mapped Allen Branch line intersects only this 12-digit unit
facts.notes: The area is that of the whole HUC 12, not of Allen Branch's own drainage. WBD lists the next unit downstream as 051301030401 (Meadow Creek–Cumberland River).

facts.label: Watershed (HUC 10) and subbasin (HUC 8)
facts.value: 0513010302 — Pitman Creek–Cumberland River; 05130103 — Upper Cumberland–Lake Cumberland (Ohio Region 05)

facts.label: Upstream drainage area
facts.notes: To be delineated with USGS StreamStats or lidar in QGIS, with the method recorded. No area is estimated on this site until then.

facts.label: Bedrock geology along the mapped corridor
facts.value: Upper Mississippian limestones: St. Louis Limestone at a point in the upper reach (Delmer Quadrangle, GQ-909); Salem and Warsaw Limestones at a point near the lower reach (Somerset Quadrangle, GQ-1196)
facts.source: Kentucky Geological Survey 1:24,000 geologic map service (two points queried, not the whole corridor), digitized from USGS Geologic Quadrangle maps GQ-909 (Delmer, 1971) and GQ-1196 (Somerset, 1974) by R. Q. Lewis

facts.label: Karst potential (regional)
facts.value: 'Intense' (Ste. Genevieve & St. Louis Limestones) at the upper-reach point; 'Prone' (Salem, Warsaw & Harrodsburg Limestones) at the lower-reach point
facts.source: Kentucky Geological Survey 1:500,000 karst-potential map service
facts.notes: Regional-scale classification. It indicates that groundwater flow may differ from surface drainage here; it does not show any specific sinkhole, spring or conduit on Allen Branch.

facts.label: Mapped karst features (NHD)
facts.value: None mapped on or within 25–50 m of the Allen Branch line. Nearby, NHD maps springs/seeps, sinks/rises and underground conduits — 18, 10 and 15 features respectively in a roughly 7 × 7 km box around campus
facts.source: USGS NHD point layer (FType 458 SpringSeep, 450 SinkRise) and flowlines (FType 420 Underground Conduit)
facts.notes: Absence of a mapped feature is not evidence that none exists; most karst connections are unmapped. Box: 84.66–84.58° W, 37.04–37.10° N.

facts.label: Dye-traced karst connections (KGS)
facts.value: None mapped on Allen Branch. The nearest KGS dye-trace sites are about 1.4–1.6 km from the campus address point: Correll Swallet (a dye injection site) and Weir Spring and Railroad Mill Bottom Spring (recovery springs). The nearest traced groundwater flow path is about 1.1 km from the mapped stream, and the 'Slide' karst groundwater basin lies about 1.5 km away
facts.source: Kentucky Geological Survey karst groundwater basins and dye-trace map service (KYGWKarstBasins); distances computed from the mapped geometry
facts.notes: Straight-line map distances. Dye tracing is the evidence that shows where karst water actually goes, but no trace has been run from or to Allen Branch, so its groundwater connections remain unknown — not 'unconnected'. In the wider 20 × 19 km area around campus, KGS maps 61 dye-trace sites, 47 traced flow paths and 5 karst groundwater basins.

facts.label: Surrounding land cover
facts.notes: NLCD 2021 can be viewed on the map. Land-cover percentages will be calculated only after the drainage area is delineated. Nearby land use is not evidence of what reaches the stream.

facts.label: Monitoring stations on Allen Branch
facts.source: Water Quality Portal station search for HUC 051301030204; USGS gage layer
facts.notes: The same HUC 12 contains registered Kentucky Division of Water locations on Pitman Creek (CRW023 'Pitman Creek at Cabin Hollow Road'; CRW024 'Pitman Creek downstream of Somerset WWTP') and three U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, Nashville District locations (two stream, one reservoir). Registration does not mean current sampling.

facts.label: Campus access point (coordinates)
facts.notes: Not the same as the campus street address. Every portal map is centered on 808 Monticello Street (see 'Campus center point'); a GPS position for the actual creek access point will be recorded on the first faculty-led visit.

facts.label: Habitat
facts.notes: To be documented with canopy-cover measurements and photographs at defined stations.

facts.label: Cyanobacteria at Allen Branch
facts.notes: Allen Branch is not a documented bloom site. Whether benthic cyanobacteria occur here is an open question for student research.

investigation_tasks.summary: Record a GPS position (with accuracy) for the safe access point used by classes, plus the route and any permissions needed.
NHD names the flowline 'Allen Branch' (GNIS 00485848). Still to do: confirm that the channel reached from campus is this mapped line, and check county and local sources for other names.
Delineate the basin above defined sampling points with USGS StreamStats; record date, tool version and the pour-point coordinates.
NHD maps Allen Branch joining Sinking Creek, which flows to Pitman Creek. Field verification of the junction and of flow continuity at different seasons is pending.

documentation.label: Mapped path on the site map

investigation_tasks.summary: NHD routes the mapped path into Lake Cumberland on the Cumberland River (Ohio River basin). Surface mapping only.
After delineation, summarize NLCD and Cropland Data Layer classes inside the basin in QGIS. Report areas with their data year and resolution. Land cover alone will not be used to infer pollution.
Inventory pipes, ditches and culverts entering the channel during a dry-weather walk; photograph and GPS each one. Possible inputs are listed as possible until flow is observed.

KGS maps place the corridor on Mississippian limestones with 'intense' to 'prone' karst potential. KGS dye traces exist about 1–2 km away (nearest flow path about 1.1 km from the stream), but none involves Allen Branch, and NHD maps no spring, sink or conduit on it. Next: look for losing or gaining reaches in the field; any dye trace would be a project for qualified investigators.
Choose safe, repeatable stations (for example upstream, near campus, and above the Sinking Creek junction), each with a code, GPS position and photo.
First faculty-led reconnaissance: confirm channel location, flow state, canopy, substrate and access, and record the visit as a field observation.
